_README: Preset for the onset-asynchrony yes/no task (seqsfg/asynchrony.py).
Two sections, as in exposure_pilot.json. 'config' is an ordinary seqsfg Config and is hashed
exactly like any other, so nothing about pilot_config.json / wide_step_config.json changes.
'asynchrony' holds this task's own parameters; they are deliberately NOT Config fields,
because adding fields to Config would change the hash of every configuration already run.
What differs from pilot_config.json, and why:
figure_band_channels 13 -> null   elements are drawn from the WHOLE pool, so a chord is a
scatter like 3-7-15-16-21-27-30 and has no register. A
banded chord has a pitch, and a run of them streams; that
is what made the old absent interval sound like a figure.
tone_dur_ms 45 -> 40              asked for, and it is what the 20 ms rung is measured against
(20 ms is exactly half a tone).
steps_ms -> 0,4,8,12,16,20        an even ladder to the requested limit.
iei 300-333 -> 340-420 ms         a 20 ms step needs 2*((N-1)*20+40) = 320 ms of element
footprint, so elements would collide at the old rate. The
wider jitter also swamps what is left of the per-channel
inter-onset-interval cue.
n_elements 9 -> 8, interval 4000 -> 4300   what fits at that rate without ever clipping the
jitter.
tones_per_channel 26 -> 28        holds per-channel occupancy at 0.26, as in the pilot.
figure_anchor_seed -> null        a FRESH figure every trial. This experiment measures where
binding fails, not what a listener can learn; cross-trial
learning is exposure_pilot.json's experiment.
The two-interval fields (main_variants, control_cells, practice_cells, trials_per_condition)
are not used by this task. They are kept valid so the file is a legal Config and every other
command still runs on it.
